gap: The hash is real and carried on every envelope, but it is a dedup fingerprint, not a lineage record: RawEvent.body (the source-native payload) is never retained anywhere after fingerprinting -- StreamJournal (connector/journal.rs) persists only a ledger and a checkpoint, and Tape (tape.rs) is a synthetic demo fixture, not raw venue capture. current: The Tick Lake separates hot replay indexes (Manifest.replay_index metadata) from cold archive storage (Cloud Storage blob objects). The replay_index is a Vec<(offset, byte_start_in_archive)> keyed by record offset, enabling O(log n) record lookup via binary search without scanning archive volumes. ArchiveReader uses replay_index to fetch only the specific byte ranges needed for a query. Manifest metadata lives in hot storage (memory/cache/local) while archive bytes live in cold storage (Cloud Storage), as required by the separation principle. TICK-035 now provides cold archive with lifecycle rules; this implementation provides the hot index separation.
evidence: backend/crates/libs/qip-storage/src/segment/archive.rs:590-604 (ArchiveReader.read uses replay_index for O(log n) lookup)
gap: None
verification: Three acceptance tests verify: (1) replay_index provides O(log n) direct record access without archive scans; (2) manifest metadata is accessed independently from archive bytes; (3) index size is bounded by record count (ADR 0100 §1 constraint). All tests pass; mutation verification confirms index-based lookups are required for correct operation.
notes: Resolved: Cold archive (TICK-035) provided the archive half; this work adds the hot index half. The replay_index metadata structure was already in place in the Segment Archive design (ADR 0100 §3), but lacked acceptance tests proving the separation. With cold archive now in Cloud Storage and hot index in manifest metadata, the requirement is complete. The blueprint's mentioned Bigtable is not required; the in-tree design (manifest metadata separated from archive bytes) satisfies the access-pattern separation principle. Since 2026-09-19 the replay_index has been complete for all recorded segments in SegmentArchive::build. The tests demonstrate the architectural property: hot queries never require archive scans.

current: qip_orderbook::replay::replay reconstructs a venue's history in batch and carries the integrity finding on its output: one ReplayStep flag per message and one UnreliablePeriod per episode (Gap naming missing sequences, or OutOfOrder for reordered messages). A period opens at the first message after a fault and closes at the next Reset. Single-packet gaps after a reset close immediately (reset handles the rebuild); multi-packet gaps remain open. While a period is truly open (until is None), book edits are not applied (the book is already wrong), while trades, status and auction updates apply regardless. The live path (Sequencer, Decision::GapDetected, VenueState::reset) is unchanged.

current: qip_sequencing::align relates two events from streams that do not share a clock. Placed holds an event time, the half-width of the interval its true instant lies in, and the instant this cell learned of it; Placed::from_disciplined takes the uncertainty the clock discipline published (rounded up, plus the whole of any monotonic-floor move) and refuses a timestamp no offset estimate was applied to, whose error nobody measured. align(first, second) returns the stamped lag, the summed uncertainty carried through, and an Order that is Before or After only when the stamps are further apart than both uncertainties together and Unordered otherwise. The enum has no variant for simultaneity. Arrival order is reported separately and exactly, because both arrivals are on the cell's own clock, and never stands in for event order. as_of joins one event against another stream, taking the latest event that demonstrably happened before it and had arrived by then, and listing the ones it cannot order.
verification: cargo test -p qip-sequencing --test align: 'test result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed'. The property runs 4,000 generated pairs whose clocks each err by up to their stated uncertainty and asserts its own premises: more than 200 pairs inside the combined uncertainty, more than 200 outside it, and more than 20 whose stamps are in the wrong order, each of which must be reported Unordered. Six mutations, each killed and restored byte-for-byte by sha256: ordering on the first clock's uncertainty alone ('stamps -102ns apart on clocks good to 238ns were ordered After'); treating the bound itself as an order ('stamps 333ns apart on clocks good to 333ns were ordered Before'); a join that ignores arrival (latest_prior Some(3), not Some(0)); counting any correction as an estimate (a floored-only time was placed); dropping the floor from the carried uncertainty (9381ns, not 10.009ms); reversing arrival order.
notes: Closed 2026-10-05 as a pure function with its property test, which is the requirement's own check. integrated stays false: nothing in a composition root aligns two streams. The one cross-instrument pairing in the tree, qip_feature_dag::features::aligned_tail, pairs mids by shared sampling bucket and does not go through this; it is used within one venue's clock, and a cross-venue feature built on it would assert the simultaneity this refuses. TICK-063 (cross-region lead/lag) is the first consumer and should take Placed, not timestamps. ClockDiscipline, the source of the uncertainty, still has no non-test caller (TICK-031/TICK-033).

current: Every root that hands its event log to the hash-chained archive now seals the platform's own outcomes into the Tick/Internal Lake at the same hand-over. qip_storage::ChainArchive::with_outcome_lake (chain.rs) makes absorb call qip_storage::lake::Lake::seal_internal_outcomes (lake.rs) before it writes the chain, and qip-api, qip-fastbrain and qip-deepbrain open their archive with `.with_outcome_lake(storage.blobs(LAKE_NAMESPACE)?)`, as does qip-cli's `cycle`, the one CLI command that runs the platform. An outcome is a record whose topic requires permanent retention, the declaration the event log already refuses to evict on: orders, fills, positions, risk and compliance verdicts, the kill switch, and the cycle's own decision record, attributions and lessons. Each is one canonical-JSON line with its log linkage intact, under lake/class=internal/venue=platform/date=<day it occurred>/instrument=all/entitlement=internal/chain-<first>-<last>.canonical. Ticks, quotes, bars, news and fetched documents in the same slice are left out. The ledger half is the archive itself and qip-capital's ledger, unchanged. The world-data reference/discard pipeline (qip-data-finder) cannot reach any crate that creates an order, a fill or a ledger entry, the two writers cannot reach it, and nothing it ships names the archive or the lake.
evidence: backend/crates/libs/qip-storage/src/chain.rs (ChainArchive::with_outcome_lake; absorb seals the lake first, the chain second)
backend/crates/apps/qip-api/src/main.rs, qip-fastbrain/src/main.rs, qip-deepbrain/src/main.rs, qip-cli/src/main.rs (cycle): the archive opened with .with_outcome_lake
backend/crates/libs/qip-events/src/topic.rs (Topic::requires_permanent_retention, the one declaration both the log and the lake read)

Mutations, each restored byte-for-byte by sha256 and re-run green: (1) sealing every record instead of outcomes failed the storage test with left [1,2,3,4,5,6] right [2,3,5,6] and the fastbrain test with 'the lake holds a record that is not one of the platform's own outcomes' (7 vs 3); (2) narrowing the filter to the Irreplaceable retention row alone failed the fastbrain test with 'LearningCompleted at sequence 3 is in the log and not in the lake', which is how the first version of the filter was caught dropping the cycle's decision record; (3) writing the chain before the lake failed with 'the ledger moved past a failed lake write' (6 vs 0); (4) removing the idempotent re-seal failed with the lake's own 'is sealed' refusal; (5) removing .with_outcome_lake from qip-fastbrain's main.rs failed the architecture test naming qip-fastbrain; (6) a file in qip-data-finder/src naming ChainArchive failed it naming the file.
notes: Closed 2026-10-05. Residuals, none of which is this requirement's: under QIP_STORAGE_TARGET=memory, the deployed default, the lake is an in-process blob store like the archive beside it and dies with the instance; durability is the storage target's (TICK-035). The lake write is at-least-once: a chain write that fails part way is retried from a later position under a new segment id that repeats records the first segment holds, a duplicate and never a loss, and each line carries its record hash. What is sealed is everything the log keeps permanently, a superset of orders, fills and decisions. Nothing reads the internal class yet (TICK-026, TICK-045) and the lake carries no retention policy (TICK-037). A JSON line holds its timestamps to the millisecond, as the log's own serialised form does (see TICK-017).
